headline: Wall Street selling deepens: Nasdaq -2.4%, Nvidia -6.0%, Intuit -8.3%; JSE All Share closes 1.5% lower
summary: The JSE All Share closed at 104,638.77 and the Top 40 at 96,832.98 on 20 Nov 2026, 1.5% and 1.6% lower on the day and about 7% lower on the week (LRC Market Dashboard, Yahoo Finance). By 17:58 SAST the S&P 500 had slipped to 7,086.73 (-1.2%) and the Nasdaq to 23,308.17 (-2.4%), leaving both 6–7% lower on the week, with Nvidia down 6.0% and Intuit down 8.3% after its outlook cut. The rand was at R17.46 per dollar, 4.2% weaker than on 13 Nov, and gold at $3,556.10 was 8.5% lower on the week.

items.title: Intuit down 8.3% to $284.41 as the sell-off after its outlook cut deepens
items.summary: First-quarter (to 31 Oct) revenue rose 12% to $4.35bn, ahead of the $4.31bn estimate, but full-year revenue guidance was cut to $23.08–23.37bn from $23.28–23.51bn because of weaker Credit Karma, and second-quarter guidance of $4.93–4.95bn is below the $5.11bn consensus; Intuit is also selling Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68bn (Intuit 8-K and press release, 19 Nov 2026). The share was 4.2% lower at 16:57 SAST and 8.3% lower at $284.41 by 17:58 SAST (LRC Stock Scanner, 20 Nov 2026). The LRC Watchlist (14 Nov) lists Intuit as BUY with a $426 fair value; the share is now about 33% below that level, and the rating is unchanged.

items.title: Selling picks up: S&P 500 7,086.73 (-1.2%), Nasdaq 23,308.17 (-2.4%)
items.summary: At about 17:58 SAST on 20 Nov 2026, an hour after the open, the S&P 500 had turned from a 0.1% gain to a 1.2% loss against Thursday's 7,175.83 close, and the Nasdaq Composite was 2.4% below 23,879.20, led by technology shares. On the week the S&P 500 is 6.3% lower and the Nasdaq 7.3% lower (week-ago closes 7,561.67 and 25,136.27). The US 10-year Treasury yield was 4.95%, down from 5.15% a week ago (LRC Market Dashboard, Yahoo Finance, 20 Nov 2026).
